items.stem: When mapping a current process, what is the most common mistake?

options.text: Documenting the ideal process instead of the one actually followed
options.rationale: Correct: an SOP must start from reality, not the intended-but-ignored version.

options.text: Using too many colours in the diagram
options.rationale: Diagram styling is not the core risk.

options.text: Mapping too few steps to fit on a page
options.rationale: Page fit is not the mapping error that matters.
Naming actors is good practice, not a mistake.

items.stem: Which TWO make an SOP usable by a new hire? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Steps written without assuming prior knowledge
options.rationale: Correct: SOPs should not assume context a new hire lacks.
Undefined jargon blocks a new reader.

options.text: Omitting exceptions to keep it short
options.rationale: Missing edge cases cause failures in practice.

items.stem: Why assign an owner and review cadence to an SOP?

options.text: So the procedure is kept current instead of going stale
options.rationale: Correct: without ownership, procedures drift from reality.

options.text: To restrict who can read it
options.rationale: Ownership is about maintenance, not access control.

items.explanation: Correct: without ownership, procedures drift from reality.
